name: Capably Digital Email Validation and Blocklist
author: Capably Digital

sections.description:
Take control of your email validation and blocking needs. Easily set up email blocklists and mx checking on WordPress email functions to reduce bounce rates and unwanted signups, and reduce the reliance and charges from third party APIs.

Features

  • Email blocklist – Add email addresses and domains to a blocklist to stop users from spamming your site.

  • Check MX records – Make sure that an email address has valid MX records before sending email.

  • Monitor only mode – The plugin will allow all email and just log the details (where configured) so you can assess the usefulness of the plugin and ensure no false positives.

  • Strictness control – Decide what you want the plugin to do when it can’t parse an email record when sending email.

  • External list synchronization – Keep your blocklist up to date by pulling in from a remote URL and set up an automated schedule. Tested with lists with over 250k domains on basic shared hosting (although your milage may vary).

  • Logging – Decide when you want to store the what, when and why an email was allowed or blocked.

  • Multisite support – Multisite networks are fully supported, with each site being treated independently to manage their own blocklist and settings.

  • Define your settings through constants – Add some code to wp-config.php to define constants so that you have full control if others have access to your site(s). Find out how in the documentation.

  • Expandability – Use the hooks that are exposed to expand the plugin and add your own functionality. Find out more in the documentation.

Pro Features

The free version is fully usable, but additional functionality is available in Capably Digital Email Validation and Blocklist Pro. If you feel like upgrading, it can be done in your WordPress dashboard from the free version.

  • Set a default action – Choose whether you want the plugin to block or allow an email address when it’s not present in the blocklist. Useful for running members sites where you can run a strict whitelist for self service user registration.

  • Email address validation – Check an email addresses parent domains, collapse plus addresses and set minimum lengths for both the local part and domain.

  • Sync multiple lists – Configure multiple list sources that will be combined and synchronized, with some of those being whitelists to ensure nothing is blocked you don’t want to.

  • Check A records – If the MX record check fails, you can also check for a valid A record, which can be used as a fallback under the specifications.

  • Scrub emails – When an email address is found to be invalid, remove it from the email being sent while keeping the valid recipients in place if the email is still valid.

  • Log granularity – Decide what to log and whether to anonymise the data, from subject to email addresses and names to the email body itself.

  • Automatic log deletion – Automatically delete logs to assist with complying with data protection regulation.

  • Front end shortcode – Display a message on the front end of your website if a users email address is on the blocklist. Add it to front end account pages where normal users don’t have access to WP Admin. Find out more in the documentation.

Compatibility

Because our plugin hooks into core WordPress functions, it’s compatible with all plugins that use the functions that WordPress provides, including popular storefront, social media and mailing list plugins.
sections.installation:
1. Download the .zip file and upload it to your site, or install from the “Plugins” page in your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Enable the plugin in the “Plugins” section of your WordPress dashboard
  3. By default only mx checking will be performed at mail-time as the blocklist is set up but empty.
  4. Head to the “Email Validation” section of your WordPress side bar to configure the plugin’s blocklist and other settings.
sections.faq:
How does a blocklist and/or mx record checking reduce bounce rates?

Bounce rates are an indicator of how an SMTP service sees you as a customer, and if your bounce rates get too high it can impact both your inbox placement and whether a provider is willing to continue doing business with you. For the most part, SMTP services don’t do their own checks to make sure that you’re sending to an email address that makes sense beyond the basics, and will treat an email address where there are no email servers (mx records) as a “hard bounce” that dings you in your providers eyes. Similarly, a blocklist lets you block particular domains and email addresses (for example those that are known to be disposable email addresses) to avoid sending to email addresses that are unlikely to remain monitored.

What happens when an email or domain is blocked?

It depends at which stage the block takes place:

  • During email validity checks (hooking into the WordPress is_email filter) the user will be presented with a message advising their email address isn’t valid, the same as they would if they used a nonsensical address.
  • During email sending (hooking into the WordPress pre_wp_mail filter) the email will not be sent.

You can decide which checks take place when in the settings page in your WP Admin, by default the blocklist is checked in both of the situations above, and checks to ensure valid mx records are performed on email sending.

Do email entries override domain entries?

Yes, they do. Since email address entries are more specific than domains, those take priority where they exist. This allows you to do things like block an entire domain, but allow a specific email address.

Can I manually override a domain from an external list?

Yes, you can. Simply add the instruction you want the plugin to follow in the Manage Domains page of the plugin’s settings, and it will honour that instruction because the implementation for syncing external lists is designed not to override your choices.

Does syncing an external list mean my database will keep growing?

No, the implementation for syncing external lists cleans up after itself by removing domains that were added that are no longer part of the list, to keep things manageable.

Will checking MX records slow down my site?

That depends on your setup. If you’re using a mailing plugin that relegates email sending to WP-Cron, then it’s unlikely to (but it also depends on where the plugin does this relegation in the process), otherwise, the mx check takes place during the page processing, which can take a moment, but generally not more than sending the email itself.

I have an issue that’s not listed, what do I do?

While we’ve tried to test as much as possible, it’s always possible that a plugin has bugs (whether that’s a missed error or something specific to your environment). If you have an issue we recommend enabling logging, which will generally tell you why the plugin blocked an email. If you still have issues, head to the plugin support forum and leave a message, and we’ll do our best to work with you to solve any issues you have.

Don’t forget, that if you’re having issues, others may too, so let us know!
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

First full release

  • [bugfix] Added cron job init to activation hook to restore automated functionality if settings dictate.
  • [bugfix] Fix blocklist logic to allow for extremely large lists (e.g. > 250,000 domains on shared hosting).
  • [bugfix] Add link in list pages where there are no results in the current view to go to “page 1” if not already there.
  • [bugfix] Correct mobile responsiveness on all pages.
  • [feature] Add actions and filters to allow customisation of email logs.
  • [feature] Add monitor only option so that the plugin doesn’t block email in pre_wp_mail.
  • [feature] Add option so an administrator can decide whether a failure to parse an email address in pre_wp_mail means an email is rejected.
  • [feature] Add Blocklist check section in settings so that an administrator can check an email address or domain’s blocklist check result.
  • [feature] Add MX check section in settings so that an administrator can check a domains MX check result.
  • [general] Remove “deactivation” option from cleanup settings, where set to this this will now be taken as “uninstall”.
  • [general] Code refactoring and optimisation.
  • [general] Added Freemius integration and launched freemium plugin.
  • [general] Rebuild settings page(s) to allow users to more easily find the settings they need and allow for fremium functionality.

0.2.0

Initial release on WordPress.org
